statements.label: thm:density
statements.text: Let $f\in\Z[x]$ be irreducible over $\Q$, of degree $d$ with $4\le d\le8$, and put $k=d-2$. If \eqref{eq:local-admissibility} holds, then \[ S_{f,k}(X)=c_{f,k}X+o_f(X),\qquad c_{f,k}=\prod_p\left(1-\frac{\rho_f(p^k)}{p^k}\right)>0. \] No primitivity or sign condition on the leading coefficient is required.

statements.label: cor:all-degrees
statements.text: Let $f\in\Z[x]$ be irreducible over $\Q$ of degree $d\ge4$, and put $k=d-2$. If $f$ has no fixed prime $k$th-power divisor, then \[ S_{f,k}(X)=c_{f,k}X+o_f(X),\qquad c_{f,k}=\prod_p\left(1-\frac{\rho_f(p^k)}{p^k}\right)>0. \]

statements.name: Separable products and simultaneous values
statements.label: cor:separable-products
statements.text: Fix an integer $k\ge2$. Let $F\in\Z[x]\setminus\{0\}$ be separable over $\Q$, with every nonconstant irreducible factor of degree at most $k+2$. If $\rho_F(p^k)<p^k$ for every prime $p$, then \[ S_{F,k}(N)=c_{F,k}N+o_{F,k}(N),\qquad c_{F,k}=\prod_p\left(1-\frac{\rho_F(p^k)}{p^k}\right)>0. \] More generally, let $\mathbf F=(F_1,\ldots,F_r)$, with $r\ge1$, be a fixed family of nonzero integer polynomials, each separable over $\Q$ with all nonconstant irreducible factors of degree at most $k+2$. Factors may be shared by different $F_i$. Put \[ \Omega_p=\{a\in\Z/p^k\Z:p^k\mid F_i(a)\text{ for at least one }i\}. \] Let $S_{\mathbf F,k}(N)$ count the integers $1\le n\le N$ for which every $F_i(n)$ is $k$-power-free. If $\#\Omega_p<p^k$ for every prime $p$, then \[ S_{\mathbf F,k}(N)=c_{\mathbf F,k}N+o_{\mathbf F,k}(N),\qquad c_{\mathbf F,k}=\prod_p\left(1-\frac{\#\Omega_p}{p^k}\right)>0. \]

statements.label: prop:large-prime-tail
statements.text: Let $f\in\Z[x]$ be primitive and irreducible, with positive leading coefficient and degree $4\le d\le8$. Put $k=d-2$. There exists $\delta=\delta_f>0$ such that \[ \#\{n\in\Z:X<n\le2X,\ p^k\mid f(n) \text{ for some prime }p>X\} \ll_f X^{1-\delta}. \]

statements.name: Sieve transfer
statements.label: prop:sieve-transfer
statements.text: Let $f\in\Z[x]$ be irreducible over $\Q$, of degree $d\ge2$, and let $k\ge2$. Suppose that $\rho_f(p^k)<p^k$ for every prime $p$. Write \[ f=s c g,\qquad s\in\{-1,1\},\quad c\in\N, \] where $c$ is the positive content of $f$ and $g\in\Z[x]$ is primitive with positive leading coefficient. Assume that \begin{equation} T_g(X):=\#\{n\in\Z:X<n\le2X,\ p^k\mid g(n) \text{ for some prime }p>X\}=o_{g,k}(X). \end{equation} Then \[ S_{f,k}(N)=c_{f,k}N+o_{f,k}(N),\qquad c_{f,k}=\prod_p\left(1-\frac{\rho_f(p^k)}{p^k}\right)>0. \]

statements.label: thm:affine-counting
statements.text: Fix integers $1\le r\le N$, a degree bound $e_0$, a constant $C$, positive coordinate weights $\omega_l$, and positive numbers $\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_r$. For $X\ge2$, let $S\subseteq\Z^N$ satisfy \[ |z_l|\le C X^{\omega_l}\quad(z\in S), \] and suppose $S$ lies on an algebraic set $Z$ of degree at most $e_0$ and dimension at most $r$. Assume the following uniform alternative. For every fixed degree bound $e$, each irreducible subvariety $A\subseteq Z$ defined over $\Q$, of degree at most $e$ and dimension $h>0$, meeting $S$, satisfies either \begin{equation} |S\cap A|\ll_{e,\alpha} X^\alpha \quad\text{for every fixed }\alpha>0, \end{equation} or \begin{equation} H_A(T)\ge \frac{T^h}{h!\delta_h^h}-C_eT^{h-1} \quad(T\ge1). \end{equation} The constants in these alternatives are uniform in $X,Z,S,A$. Put $E_h=\max_{h\le s\le r}\delta_s$. Then, for every $\eps>0$, \begin{equation} |S|\ll_\eps X^{E_1+\cdots+E_r+\eps}. \end{equation} The implied constant depends only on the fixed data and the uniform constants in the hypotheses. In particular, no bound on the coefficients initially defining $Z$ is required.

statements.label: prop:archimedean-cuts
statements.text: Fix positive upper exponents $\eta_+,b_+$. Consider a paired box as in Lemma \ref{lem:paired-boxes}, with integer coordinates satisfying \[ |x_i|\ll X^{\eta_+/d},\qquad |y_i|\ll X^{b_+/d}. \] Assume that its normalized chart variables have width \(O(X^{-w})\), that \(z=1/n=O(X^{-1})\), and that the forward and reverse analytic chart functions have the uniform derivative bounds of that lemma. Let \(t_*,w>0\) be fixed rational numbers satisfying \begin{equation} \begin{split} w^{d-1}H(t_*)&> \left(\frac{(d+1)(\eta_++b_+t_*)}{d^2}\right)^d,\\ w^{d-2}\min\{H_a(t_*),H_b(t_*)\}&> \left(\frac{\eta_++b_+t_*}{d-1}\right)^{d-1}. \end{split} \end{equation} For sufficiently large \(X\), the points in this box lie on a bounded number of bounded-degree algebraic sets of the following two types: \begin{enumerate} \item a mixed hypersurface section of \(\mathcal V\), whose bicone is a prime complete intersection with one additional equation of bidegree \((\lambda,s_0)\), where \(\lambda,s_0\geq1\); \item a set of biprojective dimension at most \(d-2\). \end{enumerate} On returning to the affine equations \(a_i^kb_i=n-\theta_i\), the corresponding dimensions are \(d\) and at most \(d-1\). All number and degree bounds are uniform over the boxes and \(X\).

statements.label: prop:lattice-boxes
statements.text: For the paired boxes of Lemma \ref{lem:paired-boxes}, assume the coordinate bounds above and fix parameters satisfying \eqref{eq:lattice-parameters}. The paired boxes can be grouped into finitely many ranges indexed by $j=\ell\tau$, $\ell\in\Z_{\ge0}$, with $j\le m/d$. The number of paired boxes in range $j$ is \begin{equation} O\bigl(X^{m-dj}\bigr). \end{equation} For each paired box there are integral unimodular changes $x\leftrightarrow x'$ and $y\leftrightarrow y'$ such that all its selected points satisfy \begin{equation} |x'_i|\ll X^U,\qquad |y'_i|\ll X^V, \qquad U=u+j+\tau,\quad V=v+j+\tau. \end{equation} The matrices of these changes and their inverses have entries bounded by a fixed power of $X$.

statements.label: prop:weighted-hilbert
statements.text: For each nonzero coefficient polynomial \(f_I\), define \[ \nu_{i,I}=\operatorname{ord}_{n-\theta_i}f_I,\qquad e_i=\min_I(I_i+k\nu_{i,I}), \] and put \begin{equation} D=\max_I\{U|I|+(kU+V)\deg f_I\}-U\sum_i e_i. \end{equation} Then \(D>0\), and the weighted filtered Hilbert function of the pair image satisfies \begin{equation} H_{Y_{\mathrm{pair}}}(T)= \frac{(kU+V)^{h-1}D}{U^hV^h}\frac{T^h}{h!} +O(T^{h-1}+1). \end{equation} This is a lower bound for \(H_Y(T)\). If the function field degree of \(Y\) over its pair image is at least two, the leading coefficient in this lower bound can be doubled. For fixed weights and bounded degree of \(Y\), all error constants are uniform, independently of the coefficients of its equations.

statements.label: prop:quartic-surface
statements.text: Let $Y$ be a geometrically irreducible surface defined over $\Q$ in the rational coordinates of the arithmetic boxes. Suppose that it meets the open $a_1a_2a_3a_4\ne0$, satisfies \[ a_i^2b_i=n-\theta_i\qquad(1\le i\le4), \] and that $n$ is nonconstant and algebraic over the field generated by $a_1,\ldots,a_4$. Give the two coordinate blocks positive rational weights $U,V$, respectively, and put \[ D_0=\min(3U,2V,U+V). \] Then \begin{equation} H_Y(T)\ge \frac{T^2}{2} \min\left\{\frac{(2U+V)D_0}{U^2V^2},\frac3{U^2}\right\}-O(T). \end{equation} For fixed weights and a bound on $\deg Y$, the error is uniform in the moving coordinate changes and defining equations.

statements.label: prop:quintic-discard
statements.text: There are finitely many polynomials $\Phi\in L[t]$ of degree five with distinct critical points $z_1=0,z_2=1,z_3,z_4$ satisfying \[ \Phi(z_i)=\theta_i\qquad(1\le i\le4). \] Let $\mathcal F_f$ be this finite family and put \[ \mathcal E_f= \{n\in\Z:n=\Phi(z)\text{ for some } \Phi\in\mathcal F_f, z\in L\}. \] Then, for $X\ge1$, \begin{equation} \#\bigl(\mathcal E_f\cap[-2X,2X]\bigr)\ll_f X^{1/5}. \end{equation} Moreover, if $N(s)\in L[s]$ has degree five and distinct critical points $\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_4\in L$ with $N(\tau_i)=\theta_i$, every integer value $N(s)$ at $s\in L$ belongs to $\mathcal E_f$.

statements.name: Curve alternatives
statements.label: prop:curve-alternatives
statements.text: Put \[ g=(d-1)(k-1)+\mathbf 1_{d=4},\qquad \delta_1(U,V)=\max\{U/2,\min(U,V/g)\}. \] Fix a degree bound $E$, and let $C$ be a geometrically irreducible curve of degree at most $E$, defined over $\Q$, in the arithmetic variety $a_i^k b_i=n-\theta_i$ in the coordinates just described. For every $\eps>0$, either \[ |S\cap C|\ll_{f,E,\eps}X^\eps, \] or its filtered Hilbert dimension, with weight $U$ on $x'$ and weight $V$ on $y'$, satisfies \begin{equation} H_C(T)\ge \frac{T}{\delta_1(U,V)}-O_{f,E}(1). \end{equation} The implied constants may also depend on a fixed compact subset of $(0,\infty)$ containing $U,V$. They are otherwise uniform in the weights and in the integral coordinate changes. In particular they are uniform for the weights arising from Proposition \ref{prop:lattice-boxes}.

statements.name: Parameter choice
statements.label: prop:parameter-certificate
statements.text: For each $d\in\{4,5,6,7,8\}$, the stopping index in \eqref{eq:parameter-stop} is the one listed in Table \ref{tab:parameter-certificate}. For every integer $K_0\le z<z_d$, there are positive rational numbers $t_*,w$ such that, with $m=(d-1)w$, \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} 0<m<1,\qquad \min(\eta_-,b_-)>m,\\ w^{d-1}H(t_*)> \left(\frac{(d+1)(\eta_++b_+t_*)}{d^2}\right)^d,\\ w^{d-2}\min\{H_a(t_*),H_b(t_*)\}> \left(\frac{\eta_++b_+t_*}{d-1}\right)^{d-1}. \end{gathered} \end{equation} In particular, the cut conditions \eqref{eq:cut-conditions} hold. For \[ u=\frac{\eta_+-m}{d},\qquad v=\frac{b_+-m}{d}, \] these choices also satisfy \begin{equation} \frac3{20}\le\frac vu\le5,\qquad m+\sum_{h=1}^dE_h(u,v)<\frac{999}{1000}, \qquad m+2u<\frac{999}{1000}\quad(\text{mode }\mathsf Q). \end{equation} Moreover, for either fixed mode, every $U,V>0$ with $3/20\le V/U\le5$ satisfies \begin{equation} \delta_h(U+s,V+s)\le\delta_h(U,V)+s \quad(s\ge0,\ 1\le h\le d). \end{equation}

statements.label: cor:cyclotomic-density
statements.text: Put \[ c_8=\prod_{p\equiv1\pmod8}\left(1-\frac4{p^2}\right). \] Then $c_8>3/4$, and \[ \#\{1\le n\le X:n^4+1\text{ is squarefree}\}=c_8X+o(X). \] Consequently, for every sufficiently large real $N$, \[ \#\{n\in\Z:N\le n\le2N,\ n^4+1\text{ is squarefree}\} \ge N/2. \]

statements.label: prop:cyclotomic-central
statements.text: With $\epsilon_0=10^{-6}$, there exists $\delta_0>0$ such that \[ \#\{n\in\Z:N\le n\le2N,\ p^2\mid n^4+1\text{ for some prime } N^{1-\epsilon_0}\le p\le N^{3/2+\epsilon_0}\} \ll N^{1-\delta_0}. \]

Put $k=d-2$ and assume no prime $k$th power divides every value of $f$. Then the number of positive integers $n\le X$ for which $f(n)$ is $k$-free is $c_fX+o_f(X)$, where $c_f>0$ is the convergent product of local factors.
